concepts.name: Whisky master-blender batch-consistency judgment (composing a consistent product from variable casks by nose)
concepts.open_problem: Each cask matures differently, so the blender follows a general recipe but ADJUSTS every batch by nose to hold the brand flavour constant; the decisive 'which casks, how much, when to swap' nuance judgment is acquired only over many years and stays tacit/uncodified.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - the spirits industry is huge and Mackmyra's 'Intelligens' is an AI-GENERATED whisky, but it is explicitly human-curated: AI proposes recipes, a human still selects/signs off the nose-consistency, so the master blender's sensory judgment is not industrially replaced
concepts.app_market_check: 'whisky blending app' - DIY tools exist (Whisky Blender site to bottle your own; flavour-scaling calculators; pro cask-management software with an 'aromatic score' recipe) but they manage proportions/casks, not the by-nose batch-matching judgment; rate low
concepts.verbatim_quote: The Master Blender of the distillery is following a general recipe (i.e., so many barrels of this age, so many of that cask type, etc.) that he or she adjusts on every batch to ensure overall consistency.

concepts.name: Whisky blender's 'nose' (olfactory appraisal as the primary assessment instrument)
concepts.open_problem: The nose is treated as the most important 'device' for appraising whisky and is even formally tested in blenders; recognizing the decisive nuances and combining them is learned in practice over many years and resists formal specification.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - electronic-nose/electronic-tongue sensor arrays with CNNs can now discriminate liquor vintage and similar liquids, an industrial analog of detection, but they classify/QC rather than perform the compositional 'combine the nuances' creative judgment
concepts.app_market_check: 'whisky nosing app' - tasting-note/flavour-wheel apps exist for hobbyists; no app reproduces a trained appraisal nose; rate low
concepts.verbatim_quote: There are tests carried out on blenders' olfactory senses (the nose), as this is the most important 'device' for appraising and assessing Whisky.

concepts.name: Cognac cellar master eaux-de-vie assembly (intuiting which aromas will 'work' in a blend)
concepts.open_problem: Beyond detecting aromas, the cellar master must know how esters/acids/aldehydes/phenols interact when combined and has an 'uncanny ability to just know' which combination works - an intuitive compositional skill taking years that has no formal generative model.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - Cognac assemblage by the maitre de chai is an inherently bespoke human sensory craft; no automated process composes the eaux-de-vie blend by judgment (houses market it as artisanal/hand-assembled)
concepts.app_market_check: 'cognac blending app' - none found beyond brand 'virtual master blender' marketing experiences; rate very-low
concepts.verbatim_quote: Specialists include being an expert viticulturist, a winemaker, a blender, have a highly refined sense of smell and taste, and have the uncanny ability to just know what combination of flavors and aromas will work within a blend.

concepts.name: Solera capataz extraction-timing judgment (deciding when/how much wine to draw via venencia tasting)
concepts.open_problem: In the criaderas-y-solera fractional-blending system the capataz never extracts blindly: he tastes (venenciados) before/during/after each saca to decide the timing and volume of withdrawal that keeps the solera's character constant - a continuous tacit decision tied to each bodega's unique conditions.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - the dynamic fractional-blending decision driven by venencia tasting is a bespoke cellar-master judgment with no automated equivalent
concepts.app_market_check: 'solera blending app' / 'sherry saca app' - none found; only educational explainers; rate none
concepts.verbatim_quote: No capataz (foreman) decides to extract wine blindly.

concepts.name: Tea taster/blender recipe creation for flavour consistency across estates/batches
concepts.open_problem: Tea blenders create blending formulas combining teas from many sources to hold a consistent flavour across billions of teabags despite raw-leaf variation, requiring 9-12 years of training and constant by-palate comparing/adjusting; the discrimination judgment that sets the formula and price stays human.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - the tea industry is industrial-scale, and descriptor systems (e.g. 95 descriptors) plus e-tongue/e-nose QC tools exist, but the formula-setting and batch-matching is still done by trained human tasters tasting hundreds of cups daily
concepts.app_market_check: 'tea blending app' - hobby blend-recipe and tea-log apps exist; none replicate professional taster batch-matching; rate low
concepts.verbatim_quote: Master Blenders require 9-12 years of training and taste up to 400 cups of tea every day to ensure quality and consistency.

concepts.name: Perfumer accord composition (balancing notes into a harmonious blend by smell)
concepts.open_problem: Building an accord is an iterative art-and-science of selecting ingredients and tuning exact ratios by smell so no note overpowers another; it relies on the perfumer's intuition, memory and creativity and is done by repeated blend-test-adjust cycles rather than a closed-form method.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - the fragrance industry is large and AI tools now assist composition (Symrise/IBM 'Philyra' generates novel formulas; PerfumeLab's AI engine critiques top/heart/base balance), but these augment rather than replace the perfumer's nose-driven accord judgment
concepts.app_market_check: 'perfume formula app' - SATURATED: Formulair, Perfume Workbench, The Perfumer's Workbook/Wizard, PerfumeLab (AI), Fragrance Calculator - they do the maths/IFRA checks and some give AI suggestions, but the creative accord decision stays human; rate moderate
concepts.verbatim_quote: The precise ratio of each component is crucial - too much of one note can overpower the others, and too little makes its contribution lost, which often involves iterative blending, testing, and adjustment.

concepts.name: AI-augmented fragrance formula generation (Philyra) - the explicit AI incursion
concepts.open_problem: Even the leading AI (Philyra) is positioned to AUGMENT perfumer creativity, not automate the sensory call: it predicts raw-material complements, dosage and novelty from 3.5M formulas, but a human perfumer still evaluates and finalizes the scent - leaving the final olfactory judgment as the open human-held step.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - this concept IS the industrial AI analog: Symrise+IBM deployed Philyra to design commercial fragrances (O Boticario, 2019); flag that this part of domain B is genuinely AI-touched
concepts.app_market_check: 'AI perfume app' - exists (Philyra internal tool; consumer AI scent-recommenders; PerfumeLab AI) - this is the most AI-penetrated task in either domain; rate high
concepts.verbatim_quote: Rather than focusing on efficiency and automating tasks, the creators chose to focus on augmenting perfumer creativity through an AI that could identify patterns and predict novel combinations.

concepts.name: Nerikoh (Japanese kneaded incense) blending 'by feel' and maturation judgment
concepts.open_problem: Powdered aromatics are kneaded with honey/plum and matured in jars; the water/honey amount is adjusted by FEEL at the fingertips according to temperature and humidity, a step handled only by veteran craftspeople, and the months-long commingling/maturation that 'makes' the scent is judged, not measured.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - artisanal kneaded-incense composition is taught through long apprenticeship and tuned by tactile/olfactory feel; no automated process composes or judges nerikoh maturation
concepts.app_market_check: 'incense blending app' / 'nerikoh recipe app' - none found beyond workshop pages and recipe blogs; rate none
concepts.verbatim_quote: Because the amount is adjusted by feel at the fingertips, this step is handled by veteran craftspeople with highly refined skill and intuition.

concepts.name: Kodo monkoh / kumiko scent-discernment ('listening to incense' and identifying materials)
concepts.open_problem: Kodo trains sensory discernment to 'listen to' and distinguish aromatic woods and to identify materials in the kumiko guessing game; it is framed as structured training of attention (like studying music) - a connoisseur discrimination skill with no computational model of the holistic judgment.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - the incense-appreciation/identification art has no industrial or automated analog; it is a cultivated human sensory practice (geido)
concepts.app_market_check: 'incense identification app' / 'kodo app' - none found beyond cultural explainers; rate none
concepts.verbatim_quote: Kodo is a structured practice focused on sensory discernment, similar to studying music rather than just listening, with every element intended to cultivate a specific quality of attention.

notes: HONEST flag: this domain pair is MORE AI-touched than the v2 hypothesis would predict, especially domain B. Clear AI incursions / industrial analogs: (1) PERFUMERY accord/formula work - Philyra (Symrise+IBM, 3.5M formulas, shipped commercial fragrances for O Boticario) is a real AI that GENERATES formulas; perfume-formula software is SATURATED (Formulair, Perfume Workbench, Perfumer's Workbook/Wizard, PerfumeLab with an AI critique engine). Rated this task moderate, and the Philyra concept itself high / has_industrial_analog=yes. (2) WHISKY blending - Mackmyra 'Intelligens' is marketed as the world's first AI-created whisky (Microsoft Azure + Fourkind, ~70M candidate recipes); electronic-tongue+CNN can classify liquor vintage; AI sommeliers (WineGPT, Vivino Taste Match) exist. BUT in every spirits case the output is explicitly 'AI-generated, human-CURATED' - the AI proposes, a human nose still selects and signs off consistency - so I rated whisky tasks low (not none) and has_industrial_analog=partial. GENUINE WHITE SPACE (no-industrial-analog AND zero AI, hypothesis SUPPORTED here): solera capataz extraction-timing judgment (none/no), nerikoh kneaded-incense blending-by-feel + maturation (none/no), and kodo monkoh/kumiko scent discernment (none/no) - no dedicated app or machine found for any. Cognac assemblage is near-white (very-low/no). Tea blending is partial/low (descriptor systems + e-tongue QC exist but formula-setting is human). NET: the v2 'no-industrial-analog -> no AI' pattern holds for the bespoke/cultural sensory-judgment tasks (solera timing, nerikoh, kodo, cognac), but FAILS where a large modern industry funded automation of the composition step (perfumery via Philyra; whisky via Mackmyra) - those have real prior AI work. Method caveat: all verbatim quotes are taken from WebSearch result snippets actually seen (no page re-fetch); recorded only concepts I observed in results (R5).
